entries.content: The root cause was three defects in `parse_combinator`/`parse_selectors` in `soupsieve/css_parser.py`: (1) a leading non-whitespace combinator (e.g. `> div`) at the start of a selector or selector-list item was silently accepted instead of raising `SelectorSyntaxError("Expected a selector at position N")`, so `:is(> div)` and `:is(div, > div)` returned wrong results instead of failing; (2) at a comma, the pending relation list was not flushed into the completed compound selector, so `div > p, span` mis-associated the relations; and (3) at the end of `parse_selectors`, the accumulated relations were appended in parse order rather than reversed, which inverted the ancestor chain for multi-combinator selectors like `:scope > body > div`, breaking `:scope`/`&` matching with nested relations. The fix flushes `reversed(relations)` into the selector both at commas and at the end of parsing, and raises the appropriate errors for leading and multiple combinators. All 381 existing tests pass and the issue's examples now raise `SelectorSyntaxError` with the expected messages.
